name: Nostr
description: Open protocol for decentralized, censorship-resistant social networking using cryptographically signed messages distributed via relay servers
devStatus: Released / Active — widely deployed open protocol defined by NIPs; 250+ client apps and relay implementations; NIP-01 core stable; active NIP development for extensions including private DMs (NIP-17), file storage (NIP-96), and remote signing (NIP-46) [a]
devStatusNote: Released / Active — widely deployed open protocol defined by NIPs; 250+ client apps and relay implementations; NIP-01 core stable; active NIP development for extensions including private DMs (NIP-17), file storage (NIP-96), and remote signing (NIP-46) [a]
owner: fiatjaf (pseudonymous creator, identified as Giovanni Torres Parra) / Community-maintained [a][e]
governingBody: None (community NIP process; no formal standards body or legal entity)
stack: Multi-language (JavaScript, Rust, Go, C#, Python implementations) [b]
funding: Donations (Jack Dorsey $245k BTC in Dec 2022 direct to fiatjaf; $10M to OpenSats in May 2023) [a][d][e]
captureRiskReasoning: Overall Minimal (1): a public-domain protocol with rough-consensus community governance and no entity able to capture it. Governance & legal control (≈1): the protocol is unlicensed/public domain and evolves through the community NIP process with no formal body or IP holder [b]. Funding & key-org dependency (≈2): creator fiatjaf is influential but pseudonymous, and funding is diversified through donations and the OpenSats foundation rather than a single controlling funder [a][d][e]. Forking viability (≈1): trivially forkable with many independent relay and client implementations [b]. Regulatory exposure and track record are minimal (no legal entity; no capture-favoring events) [a].

entityAttributes.protocolMaturityStandardization: De Facto Standard (NIP process — community-driven specification via Nostr Implementation Possibilities; no formal standards body; wide adoption) [b]

name: tinySSB
description: Minimal P2P protocol for append-only logs over extremely constrained networks (LoRa, BLE) with 120-byte packet limit, GOSET feed synchronization, and mesh networking
owner: Christian Tschudin (University of Basel), with contributors Erick Lavoie, @mixmix, @nanomonkey [a][b]
license: Open source (no specific license stated in spec) [a]
captureRiskReasoning: Overall Low (2): a small but fully open academic protocol with no commercial control. Governance & legal control (≈2): developed openly within the University of Basel Computer Networks group as part of the SSB protocol family, with no proprietary licensing [a][b]. Funding & key-org dependency (≈3): a small research team led by Christian Tschudin is the main locus of activity, giving it meaningful key-person dependency, though it is university-supported rather than commercially steered [b]. Forking viability (≈2): an open, deliberately minimal protocol that others can reimplement. Regulatory exposure and track record are minimal.

references.note: GitHub repo: protocol spec, BLE/LoRa, 120-byte packets, ed25519
University of Basel Computer Networks Group: Christian Tschudin, Erick Lavoie, project description, 128-byte format
Academic paper by Tschudin: ed25519 public keys, LoRa mesh, compressed replication
Packet size discrepancy: GitHub says 120 bytes, University of Basel research page says 128 bytes. Using 120B from GitHub spec as primary

entityAttributes.protocolMaturityStandardization: Academic / Research (university research project from University of Basel; published academic papers; builds on SSB protocol family) [b][c]

name: Lit Protocol
description: A decentralized key management and compute network using threshold cryptography and trusted execution environments (TEEs) to provide programmable signing, encryption, and access control across blockchains and off-chain platforms [a][b]
devStatus: Released (Mainnet-Beta; v0 mainnet live; transitioning to v1 with LITKEY token launch) [b][e] Reclassified 2026-09-14: 'v0 mainnet live' is real production chain activity; 'Mainnet-Beta' is network branding (same pattern as Solana's own 'mainnet beta' naming), not a maturity claim.
devStatusNote: Released (Mainnet-Beta; v0 mainnet live; transitioning to v1 with LITKEY token launch) [b][e] Reclassified 2026-09-14: 'v0 mainnet live' is real production chain activity; 'Mainnet-Beta' is network branding (same pattern as Solana's own 'mainnet beta' naming), not a maturity claim.
owner: Lit Protocol (co-founded by David Sneider; backed by Lit Association) [c][d]
stack: Rust + JavaScript/TypeScript (node network in Rust; Lit Actions execute JavaScript in sealed VMs; client SDKs in TypeScript) [b][f]
funding: VC ($13M Series A led by 1kx in Sept 2022; additional funding totaling $15.2M+; investors include 1kx, RRE Ventures, OpenSea Ventures, Eniac Ventures, Protocol Labs, Collab+Currency) [c][d]
captureRiskReasoning: Overall Moderate (3), at the high end: a company-and-token-controlled network softened by an open license. Governance & legal control (≈4): steered by the Lit Protocol company and Lit Association; Apache-2.0 mitigates closure but direction and brand are concentrated [c][d][f]. Funding & key-org dependency (≈4): heavily VC-funded ($15.2M+, investors including 1kx, RRE, Protocol Labs) with the founding company essential to continuity [c][d]. Regulatory / jurisdictional exposure (≈3): the LITKEY/veLITKEY staking token and US jurisdiction add regulatory exposure [e]. Forking viability (≈4): the live threshold-cryptography network depends on staked operators, making a competitive fork costly even though the code is open. Track record shows no capture events.

entityAttributes.terms: Self-hosting + Paid (node operators stake LITKEY tokens; network fees for signing/encryption operations; veLITKEY staking model) [a][e]
entityAttributes.funds: $15.2M+ (total raised per Crunchbase; ~$20M claimed by co-founder including all rounds) [c][d]
entityAttributes.basedOn: Original (novel threshold cryptography network; blockchain-agnostic middleware interacting with Ethereum, Solana, Cosmos, and other chains) [a][b]
entityAttributes.p2pArchitecture: Mesh network + Public Blockchain (distributed network of sealed TEE nodes performing threshold cryptography; LITKEY staking on Base L2; reads on-chain state from multiple blockchains) [a][b][e]
entityAttributes.overlayNetwork: Global (Lit nodes form a global network; any node can participate in threshold signing/decryption for any request) [a][b]
entityAttributes.contentAddressing: No (key management protocol; does not use content addressing for its core function) [a][b]
entityAttributes.local-first: N/A (network-dependent; signing and decryption require reaching threshold of distributed nodes) [a][b]
entityAttributes.e2ee: Yes (core functionality: identity-based encryption where data is encrypted such that only users meeting specified access conditions can decrypt via Lit's threshold decryption) [a][b]
entityAttributes.byzantineFaultTolerance: Yes (threshold cryptography inherently tolerates up to t-of-n node failures/misbehavior; nodes run in TEEs to prevent key extraction) [b]
entityAttributes.signature: BLS Threshold signature + ECDSA (distributed key generation produces threshold key shares; supports BLS, ECDSA secp256k1 signatures across multiple chains) [a][b]
entityAttributes.permissions: Cryptographic Capabilities (programmable access control conditions: on-chain state checks, token ownership, DAO membership, custom JavaScript logic in Lit Actions determine who can sign/decrypt) [a][b]
entityAttributes.smartContract: Yes (LITKEY token and staking contracts on Base L2; Lit reads smart contract state on multiple chains to evaluate access control conditions) [a][e]
entityAttributes.assetValueEmbedding: Native — LITKEY token is the protocol-native utility and governance token used to pay for threshold signing and decryption services, and staked by node operators (veLITKEY) to participate in the network. Launched on Lit's Chronicle chain. [e]
entityAttributes.protocolMaturityStandardization: Proprietary Open Standard (published threshold cryptography protocol; company-developed with open documentation) [b]
